title: Woman severely injured by suspected drunk driver who killed North Randall firefighter
text:
The young mother has a long road to recovery after doctors had to amputate her left leg. She is also suffering from a broken spine, several broken ribs, a fractured shoulder, and several fractures in her right foot.
PEPPER PIKE, Ohio - Ashley King is severely injured after a suspected drunk driver ran into her and North Randall firefighter Cameron Duvall just before 3 a.m. Saturday.
Duvall and King were answering a roadside assistance call for a driver who had a flat tire on Fairmount Blvd. near Brainard Road in Pepper Pike, according to police. The young mother has a long road to recovery after doctors had to amputate her left leg. She is also suffering from a broken spine, several broken ribs, a fractured shoulder, and several fractures in her right foot. She spoke with 19 News on the phone from her hospital bed.
“This whole thing is a lot for me to learn to walk again and get back mobile, and they tell me I have to go to rehab and it’s going to be for months,” King said. She’s not only dealing with the pain of losing Duvall, but also the heartbreak of not being able to be there for her three young children.
Joseph Simmons, of Geneva, is charged with aggravated vehicular homicide, aggravated vehicular assault, operating a vehicle while under the influence of alcohol, and failure to maintain an assured clear distance ahead. According to his attorney, Simmons has no criminal past and his last traffic ticket was a speeding offense in 2019.
“I really think that was very not fair I mean that bond should have been way up there for two people,” Michael King said. “That’s what a father is supposed to do,” Michael King said. “I’ve been there ever since day one. I’m not going to stop now.
